Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 1–3:

Allah the Exalted said: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿When the Inevitable Event occurs, there will be no denying its occurrence, bringing low and lifting high, when the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾ up to the end [al-Waqi'ah: 1–4].

Allah omitted the response of the conditional clause in these verses, so that the mind may wander in its estimation in every direction. That is, when the Inevitable Event occurs, great terrors will arise, mankind will be divided, and there will happen what Allah and His Messenger have informed of concerning the Day of Resurrection.

His saying ﴿When the Inevitable Event occurs﴾ is like His saying ﴿The Inevitable Reality (1), what is the Inevitable Reality?﴾ [al-Haqqah: 1–2]. What is meant by this is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿There will be no denying its occurrence﴾; that is, there is no falsehood in its occurrence. Rather, its occurrence is true and certain. Belief in the Day of Resurrection is one of the six pillars of faith which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed Jibril when he asked him about faith. He said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the divine decree, its good and its evil." Allah frequently mentions belief in Him together with belief in the Last Day, because belief in the Last Day impels a person to do righteous deeds and to keep away from evil deeds, since he believes that there is a day on which a person will be recompensed: the good-doer for his goodness and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing.

﴿Bringing low and lifting high﴾ means it brings low and lifts high. That is, some people will be brought low on it and others will be raised up. Who is raised up? Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Allah will raise those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 11]. So the people of knowledge and faith are those who have elevation in this world and the Hereafter, and as for others, they are debased according to their distance from faith and knowledge.

Thus it brings low the people of ignorance and disobedience and raises up the people of knowledge and faith. How many a person in this world, high in rank and esteemed among people, will on the Day of Resurrection be among the most insignificant of Allah's servants.

The tyrannical arrogant ones will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection like ants, trampled underfoot by people, though in this world they were strutting, proud, and exalted over Allah's servants. But on the Day of Resurrection they will be debased and humiliated, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has disgraced them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 4–6:

﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking (4), and the mountains are crumbled to powder (5), and become scattered dust (6)﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 4–6]

﴿When the earth is shaken﴾ means it is convulsed with a great convulsion. For this reason He says: ﴿with a violent shaking﴾, i.e., a great shaking. Imagine that you shake a vessel containing water; how does the water move within it? So the earth on the Day of Resurrection will be shaken by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is like His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 1], and His saying: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ [al-Hajj: 1].

So ﴿is shaken﴾ means: it is agitated and convulsed. ﴿With a violent shaking﴾ means: a great shaking.

﴿And the mountains are crumbled﴾ means they are scattered about, and they sink down and become a heap of sand, poured out. For this reason He says: ﴿and they become scattered dust﴾, like the dust that you see when the rays of the sun shine into a dark room; you find this dust in the midst of the sunlight.

﴿Scattered﴾ means dispersed. These hard, solid mountains, whose rock is greater than a camel, indeed, a single mountain may be one single rock, will on the Day of Resurrection become ﴿scattered dust﴾ by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Thus the earth will be left without mountains, trees, valleys, or sand dunes, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿They ask you about the mountains. Say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105], ﴿and leave it as a smooth, level plain (106), in which you will not see any crookedness or curvature﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105–107].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 7–10:

﴿And you will be divided into three groups﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 7]. The address is to human beings in general. "Azwaj" (pairs, here meaning categories/kinds) is used in the sense of "asnaf" (categories), as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions (azwajahum)﴾ [al-Saffat: 22], meaning their categories, and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And other kinds of similar punishment (azwaj)﴾ [Sad: 58], meaning categories. So the meaning of "azwajan" is categories.

﴿Three﴾, having no fourth: the foremost (al-sabiqun), the people of the right (ashab al-yamin), and the people of the left (ashab al-shimal). Thus people will be divided on the Day of Resurrection into three categories, having no fourth, ﴿So the companions of the right — how blessed are the companions of the right! And the companions of the left — how wretched are the companions of the left! And the foremost, the foremost﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 8–10]. He, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned them not arranged according to their merit: the people of the right are between the foremost and the people of the left in rank. Allah began with them, then mentioned the people of the left in second place, then named the foremost as the third. But when He detailed them, He began with them arranged according to their merit: He began with the foremost, then the people of the right, then the people of the left. This ordered detailing differs from the unordered summary, and it is one of the methods of eloquence.

﴿The companions of the right — how blessed are the companions of the right!﴾ means that He, the Mighty and Majestic, informed that one of the categories is the companions of the right. Then He said: ﴿How blessed are the companions of the right!﴾ Who are they? Their description will come in detail, if Allah wills.

﴿And the companions of the left﴾, i.e., those possessing misfortune (dhu al-shu'm). Their description will also come in detail.

﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: these are the best of the categories. Regarding His saying ﴿al-sabiqun al-sabiqun﴾, the most correct of its grammatical analyses (i'rab) is that the first "al-sabiqun" is the subject (mubtada'), and the second "al-sabiqun" is its predicate (khabar). The meaning is that those who hasten to righteous deeds are those who hasten to reward in the Hereafter. It is as if He said: The foremost are the foremost; those who were foremost in the world through righteous deeds are the foremost in the Hereafter through reward.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 11–12:

﴿Those are the ones brought near.﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 11] Brought near to whom? To Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They are in the highest of the Gardens (al-Jinan), and the highest Gardens are nearest to the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, because al-Firdaws, which is the highest rank of Paradise, has above it the Throne of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So His saying ﴿al-muqarrabun﴾ means: brought near to whom? To Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Those are the ones brought near﴾ to Allah.

﴿In Gardens of Delight﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 12]. He mentioned their dwelling before mentioning their rank, as it is said: "The neighbour before the house." And as the wife of Pharaoh said: ﴿My Lord, build for me near You﴾ — what? — ﴿near You﴾; she began with the nearness ﴿a house in Paradise﴾ [al-Tahrim: 11]. Here He said ﴿Those are the ones brought near﴾ before beginning to mention the reward, because their nearness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is above everything. May Allah make us and you among them.

﴿Those are the ones brought near (11) in Gardens of Delight (12)﴾, meaning: in this great abode, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. He attributed the Gardens to delight (al-Na'im) because its dwellers are made joyful in their bodies and made joyful in their hearts, as the Mighty and Majestic said in Surah al-Insan: ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressing (10). So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and give them radiance and happiness﴾ [al-Insan: 10–11]. Radiance in the faces and happiness in the hearts. So they are in delight: the Gardens of Delight, the delight of the body, or the delight of the heart, or both? Both: the delight of the body and the delight of the heart.

﴿They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls﴾ [al-Hajj: 23], ﴿and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾ [al-Insan: 21]. This is from the delight of the body. ﴿And they will be given to drink therein a cup whose mixture is of ginger﴾ [al-Insan: 17], ﴿whose mixture is of camphor﴾ [al-Insan: 5]. This is also from the delight of the body.

﴿For them therein is whatever their souls desire, and for them therein is whatever they call for﴾ — this is from the delight of the body, along with the other delights Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has mentioned in Paradise. Even if there were nothing in it except that a person is made to live forever in it, not dying, and remains healthy, not falling ill, and remains young, always a youth, never growing old — and above all of that, the sight of the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿For those who have done good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. That is, beyond the best reward. "The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, explained the increase (al-Ziyadah) as the sight of the Face of Allah." O Allah, make us among those who look upon You in the Gardens of Delight.

﴿Those are the ones brought near (11) in Gardens of Delight (12) A multitude from the former peoples (13) and a few from the latter peoples﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 11–14].

﴿And a few from the later generations.﴾ It means the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). According to this view, the fewness of this community is considered in comparison with the great number of earlier nations. It does not mean that the number of those who enter Paradise from the earlier nations, taking each prophet into account, is greater than the number who enter Paradise from this community.

It has also been said: what is meant by "the first" is the first part of this community; that is, a multitude from the first of this community and a few from its last. This view is the correct one, indeed it is the only one that can be fixed upon, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." That is, half of them. ﴿Couches﴾ is the plural of (sarir), which is what a person uses for sitting and for sleeping.

﴿Woven﴾: the scholars said it means woven from gold.

Because it would not have room for them; they would have to be in rows, one behind another. But if the place is spacious, even if they were a thousand and you placed for them circular couches, they would face one another, and however many they were, if the place is large. This verse indicates that the dwellings are spacious, and so it is. For this reason, "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who looks over his kingdom for two thousand years," two thousand years, he sees its furthest extent as he sees its nearest, there is no god but Allah, how strange! But it is not strange, because Allah is capable of all things, and Paradise's width is like the width of the heavens and the earth. Who can encompass one heaven? How, when it is the width of the seven heavens, and the seven heavens are above one another, and whatever is above has a wider circumference. None can encompass this except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; its width is like the width of the heavens and the earth.

Otherwise, whenever facing is possible, it is better.

If someone were speaking to you while he had turned his back to you, would your listening to him and your love for him be the same as if he were speaking to you while facing you? No, and this is a known, observed matter.

And while reclining, ﴿there will circulate among them young boys made eternal﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 17]. "Wildan" is the plural of "walad" or the plural of "walid," like "ghilman," the plural of "ghulam."

﴿There will circulate among them﴾ — coming and going around them. ﴿Young boys made eternal﴾ — meaning: they were created to remain forever, and they are youthful boys. ﴿When you see them, you would think them scattered pearls﴾ [al-Insan 19], because of their beauty, purity, number, and their dispersal throughout the domains of their masters. Have you understood?

﴿When you see them﴾ — meaning: you see the young boys, or you see the masters, the young boys. And if you would think the young boys to be scattered pearls, how about the masters? Greater and greater! ﴿There will circulate among them young boys made eternal (17) with cups, pitchers, and a cup from a flowing spring﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 17, 18]. Akwab are cups that have handles, and abariq are likewise vessels that have handles. ﴿And a cup from a flowing spring﴾ has no handle.

And His saying: ﴿from a flowing spring﴾ means: from flowing wine.

﴿They will not be affected by it with headache, nor will they be intoxicated﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 19]; meaning, the head is not pained by it, and the intellect is not depleted by it, unlike the wine of this world, which pains the head and takes away the intellect.

﴿And a cup from a flowing spring (18) They will not be affected by it with headache, nor will they be intoxicated (19). And fruit﴾ is conjoined to His saying: ﴿with cups﴾, meaning: and the young boys will circulate among them with fruit, fruit of what they desire; for its goodness in appearance, its goodness in smell, and its goodness in eating.

A person may dislike something either because of its ugly appearance, its ugly smell, or its ugly taste. The fruit of Paradise is not so; on the contrary, it is good in its color, size, scent, and flavor. Glory be to Allah, they are brought to them resembling one another, resembling in color, size, and fragrance, but differing in taste, and this increases a person's joy, delight, and faith in the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The "ب" here indicates causation (للسببية). The "ب" in the Arabic language is a well-known prepositional particle, and it has many meanings according to context. For example, if you say: "بعتُ عليك ثوبًا بدينار" (I sold you a garment for a dinar), then the "ب" here indicates exchange (للعِوَض), meaning: this is the exchange for that, so the price is equal to the item sold and there is no difference between them. The "ب" also comes to indicate causation, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So We brought forth with it water, and with it We brought out fruits of every kind﴾ [al-A'raf 57]. Here, the "ب" in ﴿جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾: is it for exchange (عوض) or for causation (سببية)?

* Student: Exchange.

* Shaykh: Exchange? Do you know the difference between them? The meaning of "عِوض" (exchange) is that the two things are equal. Who knows?

* Student: The "ب" here is causal, O Shaykh.

They answered that the "ب" in negation is the "ب" of exchange, and the "ب" in affirmation is the "ب" of causation.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 25–26:

So foul speech does not exist there, and speech that contains no good does not exist there. ﴿Except the word "Peace, peace."﴾

As for His saying ﴿except﴾ (illa) with ﴿a word﴾ (qīlan): the grammarians call this a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), and the disjunctive exception is one in which the excepted item is not of the same kind as the item it is excepted from. Is ﴿Peace, peace﴾ a kind of idle talk? No. Is it a kind of sinful speech? No. So the exception here is disjunctive. The sign of a disjunctive exception is that you may replace illa with "but" (lakin) and the sentence remains sound. So if it were said outside the Qur'an, "They shall not hear therein idle talk or sinful speech, but a word," the sentence would be sound. Thus illa here is the particle of disjunctive exception, because the excepted item is not of the same kind as the item it is excepted from. A similar example is the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿So remind, for you are only a reminder (21). You are not over them a controller (22). Except one who turns away and disbelieves (23). Here too, His saying ﴿except﴾ is a disjunctive exception, because what follows illa is not of the same kind as what precedes it, since the Messenger, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, is not a controller, neither over the disbelievers nor over others. So illa here means "but" (lakin). This is why the fa' appears in ﴿then Allah will punish him﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 24]. Accordingly, if someone paused and said ﴿You are not over them a controller﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 22], the pause is correct, because illa here is disjunctive and not connected to what precedes it. ﴿Except a word, "Peace, peace"﴾ means: except a word in which there is greeting of peace and the bringing of joy and gladness among the people of Paradise. May Allah make us and you among them.

Now look: ﴿In lote trees without thorns (28) and banana trees with fruit piled high (29) and extended shade (30) and water poured out (31) and abundant fruit (32) neither cut off nor forbidden (33) and raised couches (34)﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 28–34]. What is with you on the couch? The houris.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 28–34:

﴿In lote trees without thorns (28) and banana trees with fruit piled high (29) and extended shade (30) and water poured out (31) and abundant fruit (32) neither cut off nor forbidden (33) and raised couches (34)﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 28–34]. How many are these? Six.

﴿In lote trees without thorns﴾ (al-sidr) is well known: a tree known for its coolness, whose shade is refreshing. But do not think that the lote tree of Paradise is like the lote tree of this world. The name is one, but the meaning differs, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do﴾ [as-Sajdah: 17]. If what is in Paradise were like what is in this world, we would know it. But the name is a name, while the meaning differs; that is, the reality of the thing differs.

﴿In lote trees without thorns﴾ means that it has no thorns.

﴿And banana trees (talh) with fruit piled high (mandud)﴾. It is said that talh is the banana tree, and mandud means full of fruit. Yet even so, what is in Paradise is not like what is in this world.

﴿And extended shade﴾: shade that has no end, for there is no sun in Paradise, there is only shade. Some of the early scholars described it as like the light that comes just before sunrise: you find the earth filled with light, yet you do not see the sun. So it is ﴿extended shade﴾, that is, extended in space and extended in time, lasting.

As for His words ﴿water poured out﴾, the meaning is water that flows continuously, always, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿therein are two flowing springs﴾ [ar-Rahman: 50], flowing always. Besides water, there are other rivers in it, of honey, milk and wine, so the kinds are four. It has been reported in a hadith that these rivers flow without a ukhdud (ditch). Do you know the ukhdud? Now, irrigation channels have an ukhdud, meaning a raised edge. We call it in our dialect, the people of al-Qassim (...), I do not know whether you know it that way? It holds the water so it does not go right and left. Paradise has no ukhdud. Likewise in this world: if there is no ukhdud, there must be a digging for the water to follow that channel. In Paradise there is neither this nor that: rivers that flow without a ukhdud. Glory be to Allah the Great! Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in the Nuniyyah:

Its rivers flow without any ditch, Glory be to the One who holds them back from overflowing.

Allahu akbar! Glory be to Him! No effort is needed, neither building a ukhdud nor digging trenches.

If someone says: is this possible? We say: do not speak. Is it possible? Affirm it. Whether it is possible or not is not the issue; matters of the unseen have no "possible" or "impossible." Affirm and do not speak. Did the Prophet (ﷺ) not inform us that Allah descends to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains?

The answer: Yes. He, may He be exalted, has absolute highness. How can He be high and yet descend? How? What is obligatory? Affirmation is obligatory, and we do not say "how" or "why." This is something above the level of our minds.

Matters of the unseen, brothers, the young and those above them, do not ask about them as long as they are established in the Qur'an or the Sunnah, because you cannot encompass them. Say: I believe in Allah and His Messenger, and continue. Here we say: the rivers of Paradise flow without a ukhdud, is this possible? Possible or not, that is not our concern. As long as it is established from the infallible one, affirmation is obligatory for us. Even in this world it is possible: if you rub your hand with oil and pour water on it, you will find that it does not form clumps, without anything preventing it, without a hollow. This is in this world; in the Hereafter it is greater. Does Allah not say about the people of Paradise: ﴿So some of them will turn to others, questioning one another. A speaker among them will say: Indeed I had a companion who used to say, "Are you among those who believe? When we are dead and become dust and bones, will we indeed be recompensed?"﴾ [as-Saffat: 50–53]. His companion in the world says: do you affirm that after we become dust and bones we will be resurrected and recompensed? Do you affirm this? See how deception works! What is the believer's answer? Do you affirm that after you die and are covered with dust, and become bones and crumbled remains, that you will be resurrected? Affirming, by Allah, more than I affirm the sun. That wicked companion says to his companion: do you affirm this? ﴿Are we indeed, when we are dead and become dust and bones, to be recompensed?﴾ [as-Saffat: 53], and he was his companion in the world. But this one, Allah blessed him with steadfastness, he remained firm and became one of the people of Paradise. So he said to his companions: ﴿Would you like to look down?﴾ [as-Saffat: 54]. Come, let us look down at my companion who used to say these things to me. ﴿So he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾ [as-Saffat: 55], at the bottom of Hell, while this one is in the highest of 'Illiyyin in Paradise. He addressed him, saying: ﴿By Allah, you almost brought me to ruin﴾ [as-Saffat: 56], that is, to destroy me, by what? By his saying: do you affirm this?

﴿Had it not been for the favour of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth﴾ [as-Saffat: 57], to punishment, just as you are now brought forth. He addresses this one in the highest of 'Illiyyin, while that one is in the lowest of the lowest, and he looks down on him: ﴿Would you like to look down?﴾ Is this possible? We used to say: it is not possible in this world, but in the Hereafter, they will affirm it immediately, without any difficulty. Yet we have found that in this world there exists something made by human beings. Now there are phones by which the near and the far speak to one another and see each other's images. Does this exist or not? It exists, and who made it? Human beings made it. How then could the creation of the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, be doubted?!

My intention with this, brothers, is that you should not consider anything that Allah and His Messenger have reported to be far-fetched. You must affirm it immediately, and do not raise objections for yourselves or others about how it could be. This is a true report from Allah and His Messenger. Say: I believe in Allah and be upright upon the religion of Allah.

Here the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿and abundant fruit﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 32]. Fruit (fakihah) is every food or drink with which a person enjoys himself, for your food and drink are sometimes necessary and customary, with which you do not take pleasure, but they are necessary for survival. The second is fruit with which a person enjoys himself, such as, in this world, apples, oranges, bananas, and many other things.

﴿Abundant﴾ means that there is no scarcity in it. At any time you find this fruit, whereas in this world fruits have specific seasons and are cut off; therefore He said: ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 33], that is, they are never cut off, at all times, night and day, although there is no night or day there, but they are everlasting.

﴿Nor forbidden﴾ means no one prevents you from them. Indeed Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿its clusters are near at hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 23], that is, what a person picks of the fruit is close. Even if a person desires a fruit above him, the branch bends down until it is before his hands. Allahu akbar! Without effort. The fruit of this world is cut off, comes in one time and not another, and is forbidden. Is it forbidden or not? It is forbidden: one cannot enter the orchard and eat as one wishes, for the owner of the orchard prevents you. But in the Hereafter, no.

﴿And raised couches﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 34]. ﴿Furush﴾ (couches) is what a person sleeps upon, plural of firash (bed). ﴿Marfu'ah﴾ means elevated. What is with you on the couch? The houris.

Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, We have produced them with a special production﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 35], after mentioning the couches. That is, the mind moves to those who accompany me on this couch. He said: ﴿Indeed, We have produced them with a special production﴾, meaning: We produced them in a strange, wondrous, and marvelous manner. He explained this production by His saying: ﴿And made them virgins﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 36]. These wives are virgins; whenever her husband approaches her, she returns to being a virgin. Glory be to Allah! ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 82]. The women of this world, when a husband deflowers a woman, that is it, she does not return. But in the Hereafter, she returns to being a virgin from the moment he finishes with her; she returns a virgin.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 37:**

﴿We have made them virgins (36), loving, of equal age﴾ ﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 36, 37] (*'Uruban*) those who are lovingly devoted to their husbands. Glory be to God! This is the perfection of enjoyment: that the wife be lovingly devoted to her husband, draw near to him, and attract him with herself. This is unlike the women of this world. When a husband comes to a woman of this world wanting her, if she is reluctant and unkempt, she exhausts him before he has obtained his desire from her. But in the Hereafter, they are *'uruban* (lovingly devoted to the husband), doing everything that brings about his love for them.

﴿*Atraban*﴾ of one age, their ages do not differ. The women of this world: one is an old woman of fifty years, and another is a young girl of fifteen years, with two years between them. The husband in this world owns no more than four wives: one is fifty, one is forty, one is thirty, and one is twenty. The ages differ. Naturally, when the ages differ, the husband's desire differs. Is that not so? Generally, he desires the young one more than the older one, so he remains wavering. But in the Hereafter they are *atraban*: their ages do not differ, they are all of one age.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿For the companions of the right﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 38]. That is: the aforementioned bliss, both of the soul and of the body, belongs to the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin).

O Allah, make us among the foremost, the first to attain it, O Lord of the worlds, for You are capable of all things. (...)

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 39–40:

﴿A company from the earlier peoples (39), and a company from the later peoples﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 39, 40]. These are the Companions of the Right (ashab al-yamin), who occupy the second rank, while the first rank belongs to the Foremost (al-sabiqun).

Concerning the Foremost, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿A company from the earlier peoples (13), and a few from the later peoples﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 13, 14]. That is: a company from the earlier peoples of this Ummah, and a few from the later ones. For the best of this Ummah is the best of its generations: the first generation, which is the generation of the Prophet (ﷺ), then the second, then the third, after which they diminish.

As for the Companions of the Right, Allah the Exalted says concerning them: ﴿A company from the earlier peoples (39), and a company from the later peoples﴾, meaning: a group from these, and a group from those.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 41–44:

Then Allah mentioned the third category, saying: ﴿And the companions of the left hand—what are the companions of the left hand?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 41], and they are the disbelievers and the hypocrites, ﴿in scorching wind and boiling water, and a shade of black smoke, neither cool nor pleasant﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 42–44]. This is what they are in, ﴿samum﴾ meaning intense heat, we seek refuge in Allah. Allah, blessed and exalted, has explained its nature in many verses. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Soon We will cast them into a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment. Indeed Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾ [an-Nisa' 56]. He also informed that: ﴿Boiling water will be poured over their heads, melting what is in their bellies and their skins. And for them are maces of iron. Every time they want to leave it, out of distress, they will be returned into it, and it will be said: "Taste the punishment of the burning"﴾ [al-Hajj 19–22]. The verses on this theme are many.

As for His saying "ḥamīm": the ḥamīm is scalding water of intense heat, so they are, we seek refuge in Allah, surrounded by heat from every side. ﴿And a shade of black smoke, neither cool nor pleasant﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 43–44]. The yaḥmūm is smoke, and Allah described it as: ﴿neither cool nor pleasant﴾. "Neither cool" as is the case with shade, and "nor pleasant" in appearance, because it is foul smoke, foul in its appearance, hot in its effect. We ask Allah for well-being.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 46–48:

﴿And they used to persist in the great violation﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 46].

﴿Yusirruna﴾ means: they would continue persistently in it.

And ﴿al-hinth al-'azim﴾ (the great violation) is shirk (associating partners with Allah), because the basic meaning of hinth is sin (ithm), and ﴿al-'azim﴾ (the great) refers to shirk. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, shirk is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13].

They also used to deny the resurrection. They would say: ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected? And our forefathers of old?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 47–48]. That is, they denied this with a great denial, saying: When our bones have decayed and become crumbled remains, will we be resurrected? And will our earliest forefathers also be resurrected? For this reason they argue, saying: ﴿Bring us our forefathers, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 25]. This is a false argument, because it is not said to them that you will be resurrected today; rather, you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection. So how do you challenge us and say, "Bring our forefathers," when the Last Day is not present today so that they could challenge and say, "Bring our forefathers"? We say: this will happen on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 49–50:

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter [generations] (49) will surely be gathered to the appointed time of a known day.﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 49–50] "The former" are of the created beings, and "the latter" are all of them. They will be resurrected in one open plain, where the caller will make them hear and the sight will reach them all. There will be no mountains, no trees, and no curvature; rather, the earth will be stretched out and made flat, so that the farthest of them is seen just as the nearest of them is seen. Now, since the earth is spherical, the distant cannot be seen, because it is lower. But when the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be leveled and become like a leather hide (adim), i.e., like a stretched-out skin, and all creatures will be resurrected on this plain.

As for His saying: ﴿to the appointed time of a known day﴾, with whom is it known? It is known with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as the saying of Allah the Most High proves: ﴿They ask you about the Hour, when will it occur? Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾ [al-A'raf 187].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 51:

﴿Then indeed you﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 51], i.e., after the resurrection, ﴿O you who are astray, the deniers﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 51]. "Astray" (ḍāllūn) in action, for they do not act; "deniers" of the report, for they do not believe it, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Verse 52: ﴿Indeed, you will be eating from a tree of zaqqum﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 52]. "Eating from a tree": this tree is of the type of zaqqum, just as you say: "a ring of iron," "a door of wood," "a wall of mud." So His saying ﴿from a tree﴾ ﴿of zaqqum﴾: "from a tree" is connected to "eating," and "of zaqqum" is an explanation of "tree." It was named zaqqum because a person, may Allah protect us, when he eats it, "yatazaqqamuhu" (gulps it down with difficulty), swallowing it with great effort; he cannot swallow it easily.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 53–55:

﴿So you will fill your bellies with it﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 56:53]. That is: they will fill their bellies with this tree, although this tree is bitter, foul-smelling and repulsive in appearance. But because of the intensity of their hunger, they will eat it as the famished, desperate person eats filth, and as he eats his own vomit. So they eat it with loathing, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿He will be given to drink of pus, which he will gulp down but will hardly swallow, and death will come to him from every place, but he will not die﴾ [Ibrahim 14:16–17]. They eat from this tree and fill their bellies with it, and there will come upon them an extremely great craving for food, so that they fill their bellies with what they detest. This is more severe in torment; we ask Allah for well-being. Yet, when they have filled their bellies with this, their need for drink becomes intense. How, then, do they drink? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then you will drink on top of it from scalding water﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 56:54]. ﴿Al-Hamim﴾ is boiling water. They drink scalding water after they have cried out for help for a long time. Allah has described this water in His words: ﴿If they ask for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass that scalds the faces. How wretched is the drink, and how evil the resting place!﴾ [al-Kahf 18:29], and the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And they will be given scalding water to drink, which will cut their intestines to pieces﴾ [Muhammad 47:15].

So reflect upon this, my brother: if it is brought near their faces, it scorches them; if it enters their bellies, it cuts their intestines to pieces. Yet they drink it eagerly. He says: ﴿drinking like thirsty camels﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 56:55]; that is, the drinking of thirsty camels that are not quenched by a little. So they fill their bellies—may Allah protect us—with the tree of Zaqqum, and they drink from the scalding water ﴿like thirsty camels﴾; that is, like the drinking of camels. ﴿Al-Hiym﴾ is the plural of ha'imah, or the plural of hayma', meaning they are extremely thirsty, so they fill their bellies. Their bellies, as in the authentic hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ): «With it is its water-skin» — meaning its belly, which it fills with water — «and its sandals». I ask Allah to protect me and you from the Fire.

This is the Qur'anic verse "This is their hospitality (nuzul) on the Day of Judgment."

This is their hospitality (nuzul), meaning this is their entertainment, in contrast to the believers, whose hospitality is the Gardens of Paradise (Firdaws): ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging (nuzul), abiding therein forever; they will not desire any change from them﴾ [al-Kahf 107, 108].

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿We created you, so why do you not believe?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 56:57]. This is a matter that no one denies: that our Creator is Allah. Even the polytheists who associate others with Allah, when they are asked, "Who created them?", say, "Allah." The meaning is: ﴿We created you﴾ the first time, ﴿so why do you not believe﴾, i.e., in your being restored a second time. Here "lawla" (لولا) carries the sense of "halla" (هلا), meaning "why do you not believe?" It was obligatory upon them, since they believe that their Creator at the first creation is Allah, that they should also believe in the second creation, because the One who is able to create at the first is able to create again, and all the more so. As Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And He it is who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [ar-Rum 30:27], and He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And that to your Lord is the final destination﴾ [an-Najm 53:42]. So when did We create you? The first time. ﴿So why do you not believe?﴾, i.e., why do you not believe that We will restore you and create you a second time? Because the One who is able to create the first time is able to create you another time.

Then Allah, exalted is He, struck a parable, rather parables, concerning that by which our existence came about, that by which our survival continues, and that by which we enjoy life. He said: ﴿Have you considered the semen that you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 56:58–59]. Meaning: tell me about this fluid that comes out of you. Is it you who create it, or is it Allah?

The answer: It is Allah, mighty and majestic, who creates it. It issues from between the loins and the ribs; it is He who creates it in the womb, creation after creation. We do not bring this fluid into being, nor do we develop it in the womb; rather, that belongs to Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?﴾ The answer: Nay, You, O our Lord!

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 60–61:

﴿We have decreed death among you﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 60]; meaning: We have determined it among you. So every soul shall taste death. O Allah, make it (death) upon truth and justice. Every soul shall taste death, without fail, even the prophets and messengers. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not grant to any human before you eternity. So if you die, would they be eternal?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 34]. ﴿We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone﴾ (60) ﴿from replacing your likenesses﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 60, 61]. That is: no one can precede Us and prevent Us from replacing your likenesses; rather, We are able to do so. Allah the Exalted will replace your likenesses, meaning He will bring you into a different creation, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And We will make you into what you do not know﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 61], and that is on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 62:

﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 62]. You have known the first creation, and that you were created in the wombs of your mothers, and that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, brought you out from non-existence. ﴿Then why do you not remember?﴾ That is: why do you not remember and take admonition? This is a rational proof from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, which He presents to His servants. Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 63–64:

﴿Have you considered what you sow? (63) Is it you who cause it to grow, or are We the causer of growth?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 63, 64]

Meaning: Tell me, you who deny the Resurrection, about that which you plant by tilling: is it you who bring it out as crops after the seed, or are We the ones who cause it to grow?

The answer: Rather, You, O our Lord! You are the one who makes it grow, that is, who causes it to sprout, until it becomes a crop, as the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the splitter of the seed and the date-stone﴾ [al-An'am: 95]. No one can split this grain so that it becomes a plant, nor this date-stone so that it becomes a palm tree, except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 65–67:

﴿Had We willed, We would have made it crushed debris﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 65], and He, Mighty and Majestic, did not say: "Had We willed, We would not have brought it forth." He said: ﴿We would have made it crushed debris﴾, meaning after it has come forth and become a crop, to which souls become attached. Allah, Exalted is He, makes it debris. This is the greatest cause of grief and sorrow, because a thing before it comes forth is not something to which souls become attached. But when it has come forth and become a crop, and then Allah sends a blight upon it so that it becomes debris, that is, broken up and of no benefit, then the regret is even greater.

﴿So you would be left in wonder [fa-zaltum tafakkahun] (65), Indeed we are laden with debt (66), Rather, we are deprived (67)﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 65–67]. Meaning: you would converse with amusement (tafakkuh bi-l-kalam), wishing to dispel grief from yourselves, and you would say: ﴿Indeed we are laden with debt﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 66], that is, the loss has befallen us through this crop which has become debris. Then you would resume and say: ﴿Rather, we are deprived﴾, meaning: this crop has been taken from us and has become debris, so we have lost it.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, moved on to another subject, the subject of life, which is water. So He said:

﴿Have you considered the water which you drink?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 68] Meaning: tell me about it. Who created it? Who brought it into existence?

﴿Is it you who send it down from the cloud, or are We the senders-down?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 69]

The answer: "Rather, You, our Lord!" Meaning: Did you send down the water that you drink from the clouds (al-muzn), that is, from the rain clouds (as-sahab)? Or are We the ones who send it down?

The answer: It is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because He sends it down from the clouds, and it remains as pools (ghudran) on the earth. What the earth absorbs, Allah, the Exalted, channels into springs (yanabi') in the earth, which are extracted by machinery from wells and flow from springs. So the origin of the water we drink is from the clouds (al-muzn), from the rain clouds. For this reason, when rain becomes scarce in some regions, water becomes scarce, the water table drops, and people need water.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 70:

﴿Had We willed, We could have made it bitter (ujaj)﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 70]; that is: We could have made it salty, foul-tasting, such that it cannot be drunk. Here He says: ﴿Had We willed, We could have made it bitter﴾ and did not say: (Had We willed, We could have made it sink into the earth) or: (We could have prevented its descent), because their seeing the water with their own eyes is one thing, but being unable to drink it is a greater grief than if it were not there at all. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wishes to challenge them with what is most painful to their souls: ﴿Had We willed, We could have made it bitter, why then do you not give thanks?﴾; that is: why then do you not thank Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for sending it down from the clouds (al-muzn), and for making it palatable, sweet, pleasant in taste, and quick to digest?

Then Allah, exalted is He, moved on to a third matter by which food and drink are made fit for use, namely fire, and He said: ﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 71], i.e., which you ignite.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 72:

﴿Have you brought into being its tree, or are We the Producers?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 56:72] The answer: Nay, You, O our Lord.

The tree of the fire is a well-known tree in the Hijaz, and it may be well known elsewhere too. It is called (al-Marakh and al-Ghifar). This tree has the property that when it is struck with flint (al-marw) or with something that gives off sparks upon friction, it bursts into flame, and fire is kindled from it. It is well known. For this reason it is said: (In every tree there is fire, and al-Marakh and al-Ghifar have become the most excellent of them), meaning: it has become the greatest of them.

This fire that we kindle, on which we cook our food, heat our water, and benefit from, is the subject of the verse: ﴿Have you brought into being its tree, or are We the Producers?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 56:72] The answer: Nay, You, O our Lord.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 73:

﴿نَحْنُ جَعَلْنَاهَا تَذْكِرَةً﴾ ﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 73] It reminds of the Fire, the Fire of the Hereafter, although the Fire of the Hereafter is superior to this fire by sixty-nine parts over the entire fire of this world, including all the intensely hot fires in it.

﴿وَمَتَاعًا لِلْمُقْوِينَ﴾ That is: for travellers, who benefit from the fire through warmth and through its use in giving direction to a place. At that time, and until recently, people used to find their way to places by a fire that they placed on a high spot, which guided the lost. The fire upon a landmark was proverbial for giving guidance, as al-Khansa said lamenting her brother Sakhr:

Indeed Sakhr is the one whom the guided take as their guide, ***
as if he were a landmark, that is, a mountain, with a fire upon its summit.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 74:

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ ﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 74]; i.e., glorify Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by this name, so say: "Subhana Rabbiya al-'Azim" (Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty). Tasbih (glorification) means that Allah, may He be exalted, is free from every deficiency and defect. So when you say "Subhan Allah!", the meaning is: "I declare You free from every deficiency and defect, O Lord."

His saying ﴿al-'Azim﴾ means: the One possessing supreme greatness. When this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Make it (this) in your ruku' (bowing)." And when [the verse] ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1] was revealed, he said: "Make it in your sujud (prostration)." Therefore, when a person is praying and says "Subhana Rabbiya al-'Azim," he should keep in mind the command of Allah and the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): the command of Allah in His saying ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 74], and the command of the Messenger in his saying: "Make it in your ruku'," so that he combines sincerity to Allah with following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (...).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 75–79:

﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars (75). And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew (76).﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 75, 76] Allah, blessed and exalted, informs us that He swears by the positions of the stars. The "lā" in His words ﴿So I swear﴾ is for emphasis and attention, not for negation, because the intended meaning is the affirmation of the oath, not its negation. This is like His words ﴿I swear by this city﴾ [al-Balad: 1], His words ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 1], His words ﴿So by your Lord, they will not believe﴾ [an-Nisa': 65], and similar examples.

The "lā" is used in the form of a negation, but the intended meaning is emphasis and attention. An oath (qasam) is the affirmation of a thing by mentioning something great, with specific particles, namely the wāw, the bā', and the tā'.

For this reason, no disobedience occurs from the angels; rather, they carry out the command of Allah and act in accordance with what Allah wills. ﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 80].

Before we leave the previous verse, some exegetes went to a strange view and said: the intended meaning of His words ﴿None touch it except the purified﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 79] is that none touch the Qur'an except one who is in a state of purity. But this view is weak, and the verse does not indicate it, because if that were the intended meaning He would have said "al-mutatahhirūn" (those who purify themselves), but He said "al-muṭahharūn" (those who have been purified), meaning purified by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So this view is weak. Had it not been found in some of the tafsir books that are in people's hands, we would not have mentioned it, because it has no value. The correct view is that what is meant is the angels.

If we say that the well-guarded Book is the pages in their hands, then the words ﴿None touch it except the purified﴾ are clear. And if it is said that what is meant is the Preserved Tablet, then likewise "the purified" may touch it by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, or may not touch it.

ۛ﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 80]

That is: this Qur'an, ﴿a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾, was sent down from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because it is His speech, and the speech of Allah Most High is revealed and uncreated.

* From this noble verse it is derived that the Qur'an is not created, because it was sent down from Allah, so it is His speech, and His speech is one of His attributes, and His attributes are uncreated.

In His saying: ﴿a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 80] there is an indication that it is obligatory upon us to act in accordance with it, because the One who sent it down is the Lord who is obeyed, the Creator, the Provider, whom we must obey in what He commands, and from what He forbids and warns against we must refrain.

﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾. The "worlds" ('alamin) are everything other than Allah, and they were called "worlds" ('alamin) because they are a sign (ʿalam) pointing to their Creator, for when a person reflects upon this creation, it guides him to the greatness, sovereignty, mercy and other attributes of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 81:

﴿Then is it this discourse that you [dare to] treat with disdain?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 81]

That is: after this clear exposition of the greatness of this noble Qur'an, do you show it leniency (tudhinun, "to soften, compromise")? That is, do you soften towards the disbelievers by it, and remain silent about its explanation and about acting upon it? This interrogation is one of denunciation, because the obligation upon one who believes that it is ﴿a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾, and that it is a noble Qur'an, and that ﴿none touches it except the purified﴾, is that he should speak plainly and declare it openly, and not compromise. Allah the Exalted has said in another verse: ﴿They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam: 9]. But this is not what happens. The obligation upon the believer is to display his religion and take pride in it, and make it manifest, contrary to what many people today – regrettably – do. You find a man among them who, when he stands to pray, is ashamed to pray, and perhaps he compromises and delays the prayer beyond its time in conformity with those who do not pray. This is a grave error. Rather, the obligation is that a person be forthright and not compromise regarding the religion of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And you make your provision [to be] that you deny [it]﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 82]. That is, you make Allah's giving to you into a denial of Him, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿They recognize the blessing of Allah, then they deny it﴾ [al-Nahl: 83]. Among this is that a person attributes the blessing of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to a means, forgetting the One who causes it, glorified and exalted is He, as in his saying: "We were given rain by such-and-such a nawʾ (the rising or setting of a star in its mansion)." That is, he attributes the rain to the nawʾ and not to the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic. This is a kind of shirk (associating partners with Allah), as is stated explicitly in the hadith of Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, may Allah be pleased with him: "The Prophet (ﷺ) led them in the dawn prayer one day at al-Hudaybiyah after rain had fallen. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Do you know what your Lord has said?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'He said: "Among My servants there have come to be those who believe in Me and those who disbelieve" -meaning they divided into two groups: a believer and a disbeliever- "As for the one who says: We were given rain by the grace of Allah and His mercy, that is one who believes in Me and disbelieves in the star. As for the one who says: We were given rain by such-and-such a nawʾ, that is one who disbelieves in Me and believes in the star."'" (...)

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 83:

﴿فَلَوْلا إِذَا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ﴾ [الواقعة: ٨٣] ﴿فَلَوْلا إِذَا بَلَغَتِ﴾ means: the soul (al-ruh). What determines the referent here is the context, as in the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted be He: ﴿إِنِّي أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّي حَتَّى تَوَارَتْ بِالْحِجَابِ﴾ [ص: ٣٢] ﴿تَوَارَتْ﴾ means: the sun, though it has not been previously mentioned, but the context indicates it. Thus the referent of a pronoun is sometimes explicitly mentioned, and sometimes known either from the context or from something else.

And (al-halqum) (the windpipe, i.e. the throat) is the passage of breath, located at the bottom of the neck, or at the lower side of the neck there are two passages: the passage of breath, and the passage of food and drink. The passage of food and drink is called the (al-mari') (the gullet, esophagus), and the passage of breath is the (al-halqum). It consists of soft, round, open rings. As for the (al-mari'), it is the opposite, being like one of the intestines. The reason for this is that the passage of breath must be open, for if its passage were closed, breathing would be severe; that is, breathing would be difficult. But by the mercy of Allah, He made this like a pipe that is soft, with round rings, so that it is easy for a person to raise and lower his head. As for the (al-mari'), it is like ordinary intestines, and food and drink, being strong, open it when they descend into it.

Allah mentioned the (al-halqum) without the (al-mari'), because the (al-halqum) is the passage of breath, and with its cessation a person dies. That is: when the soul reaches the (al-halqum) while ascending from the lower part of the body to this place, and then the ties with this world are severed, and the person knows that he has turned toward the Hereafter and has finished with this world.

﴿And you, at that time, are looking on﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 84]. That is: you look at the dying person and at what he suffers of hardships and the agonies of death (sakarat al-mawt), and you cannot repel that from him, even if you were the closest near relative to him and the most beloved to him, for no one can prevent the soul once it has reached the throat.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 85:

﴿And We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 85]; i.e., his family. That is, Allah the Exalted is nearer to the throat (al-hulqum) than his family is to him. However, what is meant is: nearer by means of Our angels. For this reason He said: ﴿but you do not see﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 85]. Allah the Exalted attributes a thing to Himself when His angels carry it out, because the angels are His messengers, peace be upon them. This is not from the category of "distorting words from their places" (tahrif al-kalim 'an mawadi'ihi), but from the category of interpreting a thing according to what the context requires. Do you know why I said this?

Because someone may say: the apparent meaning of the verse, ﴿And We are nearer to him than you﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 85], is that the nearer one is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So why do you distort it? We say: We have not distorted it; rather, we have interpreted it according to what its apparent sense requires. For Allah said: ﴿And We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 85]. It is known that Allah was not in the earth such that the obstacle to seeing Him would be that we do not perceive Him. Therefore, it is the angels, but you do not see them. So if you say: how does Allah attribute a thing to Himself when what is meant is the angels?

We say: there is nothing strange in this. Allah attributes a thing to Himself when it is the action of the angels, because they are His messengers, so their action is His action. Have you not considered the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Move not your tongue concerning it to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its gathering and its recitation. So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 16-18]? ﴿When We have recited it﴾: what is meant is that Jibril recited it, not that Allah recited it; but He attributed the action of Jibril to Himself because it was by His command, and it was He who sent it with him.

So: ﴿Then why, when it [the soul] has reached the throat﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 83]; i.e., the soul of the dying person has reached the throat, ascending from the lower part of the body.

﴿And you﴾, O relatives and friends, are looking on. At that time: ﴿And We are nearer to him than you﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 85]; i.e., Our angels are nearer to him than you, because they have come to seize the soul. Allah, blessed and exalted, has preserved the human being during his life and after his death. During his life there are angels who guard him by Allah's command; after his death there are angels who seize his soul and preserve it, never neglecting it at all. So they are close to the dead person, but we do not see them, because the angels are an unseen world that is not seen.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verses 86–87:

﴿Then why not, if you are not to be held to account?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 86–87] Meaning: then why not, if you are not to be repaid, i.e., not resurrected and not recompensed for your deeds: ﴿bring it back, if you are truthful?﴾

The answer: It is not possible. In that case, you must believe in the Resurrection (ba'th) and the recompense (jaza'), because you are not able to return the soul so that you would not be recompensed. So be certain of the Resurrection.

Then Allah the Exalted divided the dying into three categories, saying: ﴿But if he is of those brought near [to Allah], (88) then rest and bounty and a Garden of pleasure﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 88–89]. O Allah, make us among them.

﴿If he is of those brought near﴾: they are those who performed the obligations and abandoned the prohibitions, performed the recommended acts and kept themselves free from the disliked acts—that is, they perfected their religion. And "those brought near" are ﴿the foremost, the foremost﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 10], those mentioned at the beginning of the surah, the ones who hasten to good deeds.

﴿Then rest and bounty and a Garden of pleasure﴾: The exegetes differed concerning His words ﴿rest (rawh)﴾. It was said: it means ease (rahah), because the believer, although he dislikes death, finds relief in it; for at the moment of death he is given the good news of "rest and bounty and a Lord not angry" (ruh wa rayhan wa rabbin ghayri ghadban), so he is gladdened and delighted, and at that time he does not dislike death but loves to meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Without doubt this is a relief for him from the troubles, weariness, cares and griefs of this world. It was also said: ar-rawh here means mercy, as Allah the Exalted said about Ya'qub when he said to his sons: ﴿O my sons, go and seek news of Yusuf and his brother, and do not despair of the rawh (mercy) of Allah﴾ [Yusuf 87], i.e., of His mercy. This meaning is more general than the first, because mercy is broader than being mere ease or ease together with attaining the desired goal; and when the meaning is more general, it is preferable to interpret the verse according to it. Thus, "rawh" means mercy, and ease is one form of mercy.

﴿And bounty and a Garden of pleasure﴾: It was said that what is meant by "rayhan" is everything that gladdens the soul, and it is not specific to the fragrant plant of sweet or pleasant smell; rather, everything in which is the soul's ease and delight, of food, drink, clothing, marriage, and scent. It was also said that what is meant by "rayhan" is the pleasant fragrance, like the well-known basil (rayhan). Which of the two is more comprehensive? The first is more comprehensive, so the verse is to be understood according to it.

﴿A Garden of pleasure﴾: that is, a garden in which one is made to enjoy blessings; it is the abode which Allah prepared for His friends—may Allah make us and you among them. ﴿A Garden of pleasure﴾ in which a person is blessed in his body and his heart; he neither tires nor is weary, neither falls ill nor grieves, neither worries nor is distressed, but rather he is in lasting bliss. The world does have pleasure, but its pleasure is tainted, according to the saying of the poet:

"One day is for us and one day against us, and one day we are harmed and one day we are gladdened."

Such is the world: if you are gladdened one day, prepare for harm on the next day; and if you are harmed one day, you may or may not find comfort on the second. In any case, Paradise in the Hereafter is an abode of pleasure in the heart and pleasure in the body.

Ibn 'Uthaymin, Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim, on surah 56, verses 90–91:

﴿And as for if he is of the companions of the right﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 90]. They are those who performed the obligatory duties and abstained from the forbidden acts, but they have some shortcoming in the recommended acts and in avoiding the disliked acts. ﴿Then, [there is] peace for you from the companions of the right﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 91]. "Salam" means our greeting of peace; "laka" means to you, O dying person; "min ashab al-yamin" means you are among the companions of the right. The meaning is: peace is upon you while you are among the companions of the right. Who are the first group? They are the close ones (al-muqarrabun), who are the foremost (al-sabiqun). These companions of the right are neither foremost nor abandoned or lost (makhdhulin), but rather in between (bayn bayn); yet they are saved from the punishment. For this reason He said: ﴿Then, [there is] peace for you from the companions of the right﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 91].

The third category: "But if he is among the deniers, the astray" [al-Waqi'ah 56:92]. "Al-mukadhdhibin" (the deniers) refers to those who deny the report, and "al-dallin" (the astray) refers to those who go astray in action, so there is neither belief nor commitment. Who are they? The disbelievers. Every disbeliever is included in this verse, even the hypocrite (munafiq).

﴿So for them there is a welcome of boiling water﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 93]. That is: for them there is a *nuzul* (a welcome, meaning the hospitality offered to a guest as soon as he arrives), and this is their portion, and we seek refuge in Allah from it. ﴿A welcome of boiling water﴾. *Hameem* is that which is extremely hot.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 94:

﴿And the burning of the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 94]. Meaning: they will be made to enter the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim) and will remain in it forever. "Al-Jahim" is one of the names of the Fire; may Allah protect us and you from it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 95:

﴿Indeed, this is the certainty of certainty.﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 95]

﴿Indeed, this﴾ refers to what has been mentioned to you, namely the division of people into these three categories, ﴿is indeed the certainty of certainty﴾. That is: the established and confirmed certainty. And the truth of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is that people cannot step outside these three categories, which are: the muqarrabun (those brought near), the ashab al-yamin (the companions of the right), and the mukadhdhibun al-dallun (the deniers who go astray). They cannot step outside of this.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 56, verse 96:

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 96]. "Sabbih" (سَبِّحْ) means: declare Him free of (tanzih). That from which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is declared free is every deficiency and defect, or any likeness to the created. He is free of every deficiency because of the perfection of His attributes, and free of any likeness to the created. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ [Qaf: 38], meaning: no weariness or exhaustion.

As for His saying: ﴿bi-ismi rabbika﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 96], it has been said that the "ba'" (الباء, the particle "bi-") is superfluous (za'idah), and that the meaning is "glorify the name of your Lord," as He said: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1]. And it has been said that it is not superfluous, and that the meaning is: glorify Allah by His name, so that the utterance of the glorification is necessary, such that you say "Subhan Allah." As for declaring Him free in your heart alone, that is not sufficient. According to this view, the "ba'" is for accompaniment (lil-musahabah); that is, glorify Allah with a glorification accompanied by His name.

﴿bi-ismi rabbika al-'azim﴾: the Rabb (الرب) is the Creator, the Owner, the Governor (al-Mudabbir). Al-'Azim is the One possessing greatness and majesty, exalted is He. This surah, even if nothing else had been revealed in the Qur'an except it, would have been sufficient in urging the doing of good and the abandoning of evil.

At its beginning Allah mentioned the Day of Resurrection: ﴿When the Inevitable Event occurs﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 1]. Then He divided people in it into how many categories? Three categories: the foremost (al-sabiqun), the people of the right (ashab al-yamin), and the people of the left (ashab al-shimal). Then at its end Allah mentioned the condition of the human being at death, and He divided all people into three categories: those brought near (muqarrabun), people of the right (ashab yamin), and deniers who are astray (mukadhdhibun dallun). So it has encompassed everything. As Allah mentioned in it the beginning of creation, in His saying: ﴿Have you considered the semen that you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 58-59], and provision of food, drink, and what sustains them. So it is a complete surah. Therefore a person should reflect upon it when he recites it, as he reflects upon the rest of the Qur'an, but it contains great meanings. And here ends the discussion of this surah.
